passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- NHIS states D-2 students generally enroll from initial entry/foreigner registration as applicable; some D-4 categories may have a waiting period. Confirm exact enrollment date for the visa subtype.
- NHIS invoices may be delivered to the registered Korean address; maintain correct registration details.
- Insurance coverage does not mean every treatment or service is free; co-payments and exclusions can apply.
- Special premium reductions, financial hardship measures and exclusion for qualifying alternative coverage require case-specific NHIS confirmation.

passages.heading: 6. Chatbot retrieval and escalation
passages.text:
- Answer the student’s exact question in their selected language, but preserve Korean procedure names and cite an official source.
- Do not infer approval, visa eligibility, fees or document sufficiency from a generic article. Ask for visa subtype, expiry date and relevant university only if necessary.
- Escalate to human supporter / immigration or competent agency when: Uninsured urgent medical care, substantial overdue premiums, disputed assessment, pregnancy or complex health benefits, exclusion requests.
- If source material is stale or contradictory, explain uncertainty and provide the agency contact.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 3) Visiting Healthcare Providers
passages.text:
Mandatory ID check

Pursuant to the National Health Insurance Act, individuals visiting a healthcare
provider must verify their identity by presenting a valid ID card before receiving
medical services. Medical services cannot be provided without presenting an ID
card. Acceptable forms of identification include those with a photo and a foreign
resident registration number, such as a residence card, passport,
or driver's license issued in Korea. A mobile health insurance
card can also be used in place of a physical ID card.

Insurance" and present it at the reception
desk of the medical provider.

TIP. Finding a Healthcare Provider

The Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA)
offers Healthcare Provider Search by Detailed Criteria, an easy-
to-use search tool that helps visitors find the right healthcare
provider based on various search options such as region, type of

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- For life-threatening illness, injury, or loss of consciousness, call 119 immediately.
- For routine care, locate a clinic (의원) or hospital (병원) appropriate to symptoms, confirm opening hours and appointment requirements, and ask about availability of interpretation when necessary.
- Bring identification, your residence card or passport, and insurance information. Clinics and hospitals may verify NHIS eligibility through identity checks.
- NHIS gives official guidance on foreigner enrollment and exclusions, including circumstances involving qualifying alternative coverage. Verify your own coverage and payment status directly with NHIS.
- Ask the provider what portion of treatment and prescriptions is covered, what must be paid personally, and whether referrals are needed for certain hospital services.
- Keep prescriptions, visit receipts, and medical certificates if needed for university absence or insurer claims. For coverage or eligibility issues, contact NHIS foreign resident service channels.

passages.heading: 6. Chatbot retrieval and escalation
passages.text:
- Answer the student’s exact question in their selected language, but preserve Korean procedure names and cite an official source.
- Do not infer approval, visa eligibility, fees or document sufficiency from a generic article. Ask for visa subtype, expiry date and relevant university only if necessary.
- Escalate to human supporter / immigration or competent agency when: Uninsured urgent medical care, substantial overdue premiums, disputed assessment, pregnancy or complex health benefits, exclusion requests.
- If source material is stale or contradictory, explain uncertainty and provide the agency contact.

passages.heading: 3. Application or response procedure
passages.text:
1. Confirm your visa subtype, foreigner registration and NHIS enrollment status.
1. Check whether NHIS has sent a notice or premium bill to the registered address.
1. Ask NHIS about student contribution level, benefits, payment method and any available reduction/exclusion.
1. Pay premiums by the deadline and keep payment records.
1. When changing residence/status or departing permanently, contact NHIS to update enrollment status if needed.

passages.heading: Important limitations and escalation
passages.text:
No universal hospital fee, coverage percentage, interpretation guarantee, or insurer waiting period is asserted.

For immigration matters, refer students to the Immigration Contact Center (1345) for case-specific or conflicting instructions. For immediate emergencies, direct them to 112 or 119. For SCH-specific academic or housing decisions, use the current official university notice and office instructions.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- NHIS states D-2 students generally enroll from initial entry/foreigner registration as applicable; some D-4 categories may have a waiting period. Confirm exact enrollment date for the visa subtype.
- NHIS invoices may be delivered to the registered Korean address; maintain correct registration details.
- Insurance coverage does not mean every treatment or service is free; co-payments and exclusions can apply.
- Special premium reductions, financial hardship measures and exclusion for qualifying alternative coverage require case-specific NHIS confirmation.

passages.heading: 1) National Health Insurance (NHI)
passages.text:
All international students staying in Korea for six months or longer are automatically
enrolled in the insurance as local subscribers* to NHI, receiving the same insurance
benefits as Korean nationals.
* Persons who register individually rather than as company employees

NHI Registration Process

Enter Korea
Register as a foreign
resident (must register
within 90 days of entry)

Automatic enrollment in
NHI (no separate application

required)

Pay a monthly health

insurance premium
The National Health Insurance Service

(NHIS) sends a notification letter
regarding registration and payment

※ Healthcare costs may be covered through a private health insurance plan until foreign resi-

dent registration is completed after entering Korea.

National Health Insurance Premiums Calculation

The NHI premium for international students is calculated un-
der the same standards applied to local Korean subscribers,
considering each student as a single household. However,
students holding a residency status eligible for abatement
[i.e., Student (D-2), General Trainee (D-4)] and whose
monthly income and assets are below the standards set by
NHI may receive a 50% discount on the monthly premium.

NHI Information for

Foreigners

※ Short-term visitors who stay in Korea for up to six months (e.g., exchange students, trainees)

are not eligible for automatic enrollment in NHI. However, some schools require international
students to register for a private health insurance plan or a group insurance plan, so please
check in advance.

※ Failure to pay the NHI premium will result in loss of coverage and higher medical expenses.

Please note that this may also affect visa extension eligibility.

passages.heading: 1. Plain-language answer
passages.text: Eligible foreign residents, including many international students, are subject to National Health Insurance enrollment. Enrollment dates, premium calculations, reductions and exclusions vary with visa and circumstances.

passages.heading: 3. Application or response procedure
passages.text:
1. Confirm your visa subtype, foreigner registration and NHIS enrollment status.
1. Check whether NHIS has sent a notice or premium bill to the registered address.
1. Ask NHIS about student contribution level, benefits, payment method and any available reduction/exclusion.
1. Pay premiums by the deadline and keep payment records.
1. When changing residence/status or departing permanently, contact NHIS to update enrollment status if needed.

passages.heading: 4. Document checklist
passages.text:
- Passport and Residence Card
- Student enrollment certificate if requested for rate eligibility
- NHIS notice or billing statement
- Proof of alternative qualifying insurance, if requesting exclusion
- Bank/payment details for automatic payment where applicable

passages.heading: 1. Plain-language answer
passages.text: TOPIK is the official Test of Proficiency in Korean. TOPIK I assesses beginner levels (1-2) and TOPIK II assesses intermediate/advanced levels (3-6). Registration windows, exam format, fees and locations vary by test round and country.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- TOPIK I covers levels 1-2; TOPIK II covers levels 3-6.
- Paper-based and Internet-based test formats may have distinct schedules and registration procedures.
- Test registration is separate from university scholarship, graduation, and immigration rules; each institution sets applicable accepted level.
- Registration schedules and available seats are time-sensitive; always cite the live official TOPIK announcement.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Which test should I take for level 4?

A. TOPIK II is the test for levels 3-6.

Q. Can I sign up at any time?

A. No. Registration is only open during announced windows and capacity can fill.

Q. Does passing TOPIK automatically grant part-time employment permission?

A. No. Language ability is only one possible eligibility factor; immigration permission may still be required.

passages.heading: (3) Language Proficiency Requirements
passages.text:
Students may apply for the Korean Language Program without submitting any
language proficiency documents. However, when applying for degree programs,
applicants must submit official Korean or English proficiency test scores that meet
the minimum requirements set by the university (or department) they wish to apply
to.

English Proficiency Requirements

Universities usually accept TOEFL, IELTS, and TEPS scores as official English
proficiency tests.
However, applicants should check the admission guidelines of the university (or
department) where they wish to apply, as different universities may require specific
tests or score thresholds.

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- TOPIK I covers levels 1-2; TOPIK II covers levels 3-6.
- Paper-based and Internet-based test formats may have distinct schedules and registration procedures.
- Test registration is separate from university scholarship, graduation, and immigration rules; each institution sets applicable accepted level.
- Registration schedules and available seats are time-sensitive; always cite the live official TOPIK announcement.

passages.heading: 1. Plain-language answer
passages.text: TOPIK is the official Test of Proficiency in Korean. TOPIK I assesses beginner levels (1-2) and TOPIK II assesses intermediate/advanced levels (3-6). Registration windows, exam format, fees and locations vary by test round and country.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Which test should I take for level 4?

A. TOPIK II is the test for levels 3-6.

Q. Can I sign up at any time?

A. No. Registration is only open during announced windows and capacity can fill.

Q. Does passing TOPIK automatically grant part-time employment permission?

A. No. Language ability is only one possible eligibility factor; immigration permission may still be required.

passages.heading: Can I travel with a pending extension?
passages.text: Consult immigration before booking travel.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: Can I return if my stay expires overseas?
passages.text: Do not assume so; contact immigration and your embassy.

passages.heading: Can I work while my application is pending?
passages.text: No. Wait for an approval decision before undertaking the proposed work.

passages.heading: Overseas travel or visa extension
passages.text: Address reporting and extension of stay are distinct immigration procedures. Completing one does not automatically mean every other required report has been completed. Confirm the correct registered address when extending a visa.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: Can I extend after expiry?
passages.text: Apply before expiry; if already expired, urgently contact Immigration Contact Center 1345.

passages.heading: Is renewal automatic?
passages.text: No. An extension requires approval.

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

For changes in academic status such as leave of
absence or graduation, your school is required to
report the change to the competent immigration
office.

Once the immigration office receives the report,
the student is regarded as not attending the
school and will be provided with departure guid-
ance. If the student has already left the country,
the Student visa will be terminated regardless
of any remaining period of stay. Therefore, the
student must obtain a new visa to reenter the
country.

I graduated in February. Can I leave the country for
a short period and return before the period of stay
expires, since it is valid until March?

The immigration office gets notified of the grad-
uation by the school and reviews the student’s
residence status. If the student has already left
the country, the Student visa will be considered
terminated regardless of any remaining period of
stay. Therefore, the visa will be terminated.

If you plan to pursue a higher degree or find em-
ployment in Korea after graduating from university,
we recommend extending your period of stay
or obtaining approval for a change of visa status
before leaving the country.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

90

I have stayed in Korea for up to six years—which
is the maximum permitted period of stay—while
completing my bachelor’s degree program at a
university. However, I still need to have my thesis
reviewed. Can I extend my period of stay?

passages.heading: 5) Change in Visa Status
passages.text:
This refers to a situation wherein a foreign national residing in Korea intends to dis-
continue the activity permitted under his/her current visa and begin a new activity
that falls under a different visa category. <e.g., Student (D-2) → Job seeking (D-10)>

In principle, foreigners who intend to change their visa status must leave the coun-
try, obtain the new visa, and reenter Korea. Under limited circumstances, however,
a change of visa status may be allowed within Korea following a stringent review
process, provided the applicant meets the eligibility requirements for the new visa.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: Overseas travel or visa extension
passages.text: Address reporting and extension of stay are distinct immigration procedures. Completing one does not automatically mean every other required report has been completed. Confirm the correct registered address when extending a visa.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: 3) Region-Specialized Outstanding Talent (F-2-R)
passages.text:
The Region-Specialized Outstanding Talent Visa is granted to foreigners who meet
specific requirements to reside in areas with declining populations for a mid- to
long-term period. International students are eligible if they meet the requirements
after graduating from a Korean university. However, they must work and live in the
designated area during the required period.

※ The visa status will be canceled if they violate any of the visa permit conditions.

Eligible Applicants:
Foreign residents who are officially recommended by the head of the local govern-
ment in areas with declining populations (excluding those holding visas that are not
eligible for change).

Main Requirements:
➀ Holders of an associate degree or higher in Korea, or individuals whose income

from last year is 70% of the gross national income (GNI) or higher

➁ Individuals with TOPIK score of Level 4 or higher, or those who have completed

at least Level 4 of the Social Integration Program

➂ Residence Restriction Period: Five years (may move to other areas with declin-

ing populations in the same metropolitan local government after two years)

➃ Eligible Industries: Unrestricted (excluding activities that are against good public

morals and other social order)

➄ Whether Family Members May Accompany Them: Allowed (spouse and minor

children)

[Note] Guide to the Pilot Metropolitan Regional Visa Program

As a system established by a metropolitan local government, it designs a

attract essential talent holding Student (D-2) or Special Occupation (E-

Can I return to my home country during a leave of
absence from school?

For changes in academic status such as leave of
absence or graduation, your school is required to
report the change to the competent immigration
office.

Once the immigration office receives the report,
the student is regarded as not attending the
school and will be provided with departure guid-
ance. If the student has already left the country,
the Student visa will be terminated regardless
of any remaining period of stay. Therefore, the
student must obtain a new visa to reenter the
country.

I graduated in February. Can I leave the country for
a short period and return before the period of stay
expires, since it is valid until March?

The immigration office gets notified of the grad-
uation by the school and reviews the student’s
residence status. If the student has already left
the country, the Student visa will be considered
terminated regardless of any remaining period of
stay. Therefore, the visa will be terminated.

If you plan to pursue a higher degree or find em-
ployment in Korea after graduating from university,
we recommend extending your period of stay
or obtaining approval for a change of visa status
before leaving the country.

passages.heading: Can I travel with a pending extension?
passages.text: Consult immigration before booking travel.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Check the expiry date on your residence status in advance. A D-2 student who needs more time to study must apply for extension of stay before their authorized stay expires.
- Confirm continued enrollment and the university’s international office instructions. The immigration office can require additional evidence based on study progress and personal circumstances.
- Use the official Stay Extension guidance, then check HiKorea for online application eligibility or reservation. Do not assume an online option exists for every case.
- Prepare the application, passport, residence card, evidence of enrollment or ongoing study, evidence of residence, and any additional items specified for your D-2 subtype. Proof of finances, tuition payment, or academic progress may be required in individual cases.
- Submit the application through the permitted route before expiry, pay the assessed fee, and retain application/receipt information. Follow requests for supplemental evidence.
- Do not treat application submission as automatic approval; verify your status and any travel restrictions while an extension is pending.

passages.heading: What is a Stay Period Extension?
passages.text: Foreigners who wish to continue staying in Korea beyond their previously approved stay period must obtain permission to extend their stay period.

passages.heading: What is a Change of Stay Status?
passages.text: This refers to situations where a foreigner residing in Korea wishes to stop activities related to their current stay status and engage in activities under a different stay status.

passages.heading: Cases for Application
passages.text:
- When registering as a foreign resident or reporting a domestic residence as an overseas Korean with a foreign national.
- When the address of a registered foreign resident or domestic residence reporter changes.
- When applying for a stay period extension.
- When applying for a stay status change (mandatory for short-term stay status changing to long-term stay status).
- When applying for a change to permanent residence status.

passages.heading: 4. Extending period of stay (체류기간 연장)
passages.text:
A residence card is evidence of registered status. Its physical replacement is NOT the mechanism for permission to remain longer. A D-2 or D-4 student who needs to stay beyond the authorized expiry date must request extension of period of stay before expiry, with the evidence appropriate to the student and institution.

1. Check the authorized stay expiry date and current visa subtype; do not rely only on the plastic card’s appearance.
1. Ask the university international office whether it offers student-group extension or issues required enrollment, attendance and financial documents.
1. Check HiKorea for current eligibility for e-application or make a visit reservation.
1. Prepare passport, residence card, application form, fee, proof of enrollment and residence, and additional immigration-requested records.
1. Submit the application before the current permitted stay ends and follow any instructions for biometric/card updates or additional evidence.
Risk situations: taking leave of absence, withdrawing, graduating, changing universities, or ending a language program can affect the basis for student stay. Do not assume the printed expiry date guarantees permission after a change in academic status. Seek university and immigration advice promptly.

passages.heading: 1. Important rules at a glance
passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

passages.heading: FAQ 4. My ARC expires next month. Can I just request a new card?
passages.text: Not necessarily. First determine whether your approved period of stay is ending. If so, submit an extension-of-stay application before expiration.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
International students have a maximum allowable
period of stay for each degree program, so it is
not possible to extend beyond that limit. If you
have taken a leave of absence from school for two
semesters (one year) or more and have left and
reentered the country, the period spent abroad
may be excluded from the calculation of your total
period of stay.

Please refer to the table below for the maximum
period of stay when planning your academic
schedule.

Category
Maximum Stay Period

Associate Degree
Up to 3 years
(up to 4 years for 4-year programs)

Bachelor’s Degree
Up to 6 years
(up to 7 years for 5-year programs)

Master’s Degree
Up to 5 years
(up to 6 years for 3-year programs)

Doctoral Degree
Up to 8 years
(up to 7 years for 2-year programs)

I’d like to transfer to another school. I’ve already
been admitted to a new school. Can I apply for a
school transfer?

In principle, you are not allowed to transfer
between schools in Korea. You must leave the
country, obtain a new visa, and then return.

However, you may apply for a school transfer
if the reason for changing schools is deemed
unavoidable. Note that the total period of stay
must not exceed each duration of studies at the
current school and the new school. If you are
dismissed from your current school and subject to
departure, you will not be permitted to transfer.

“다른 학생들도 하고 있다”, “잠깐만 도와주는 것이다”, “현금 지급이라 문제없다” 등의 안내를 받더라도, 적발 시 모든 책임은 본인에게 있습니다.

최근 법무부 및 출입국·외국인청에서 외국인 유학생 대상 불법취업(무단 아르바이트) 집중 단속 및 조사를 실시하고 있습니다.

특히 SNS, 오픈채팅 및 외국인 대상 구인 어플리케이션 등을 통한 불법 근로 연계 사례가 다수 확인되고 있으며, 실제 출입국사무소 조사 및 출석 요구 사례도 발생하고 있습니다.

최근에는 외국인 구인 플랫폼인 Face One 등을 통해 단기·일용성 아르바이트를 연결받아 적발되는 사례가 증가하고 있으니 각별히 주의하시기 바랍니다.

1. 불법취업 해당 사례

- 시간제취업 허가 없이 근로 진행
- 허가받은 근무시간 초과 근로

- 허가받지 않은 업종·사업장 근무

- Face One 등 외국인 대상 구인 어플을 통한 단기 아르바이트 참여

- 현금 지급 형태의 무신고 근로

- 행사 보조, 통역, 판매, 홍보, 물류 업무 등 일용성 단기 근로

- SNS·오픈채팅을 통한 아르바이트 참여

※ “하루만”, “단기”, “현금 지급”, “외국인 가능” 형태의 모집도 모두 단속 대상이 될 수 있습니다.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
International students have a maximum allowable
period of stay for each degree program, so it is
not possible to extend beyond that limit. If you
have taken a leave of absence from school for two
semesters (one year) or more and have left and
reentered the country, the period spent abroad
may be excluded from the calculation of your total
period of stay.

Please refer to the table below for the maximum
period of stay when planning your academic
schedule.

Category
Maximum Stay Period

Associate Degree
Up to 3 years
(up to 4 years for 4-year programs)

Bachelor’s Degree
Up to 6 years
(up to 7 years for 5-year programs)

Master’s Degree
Up to 5 years
(up to 6 years for 3-year programs)

Doctoral Degree
Up to 8 years
(up to 7 years for 2-year programs)

I’d like to transfer to another school. I’ve already
been admitted to a new school. Can I apply for a
school transfer?

In principle, you are not allowed to transfer
between schools in Korea. You must leave the
country, obtain a new visa, and then return.

However, you may apply for a school transfer
if the reason for changing schools is deemed
unavoidable. Note that the total period of stay
must not exceed each duration of studies at the
current school and the new school. If you are
dismissed from your current school and subject to
departure, you will not be permitted to transfer.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

passages.heading: 1. Immigration Status Management
passages.text:
Foreigners living in Korea may be subject to an administrative fine or may be
faced with immigration issues if they do not complete required procedures —
such as foreigner registration, reporting address changes, visa extensions or
changes, and other immigration related requirements — within the legal deadline.
Therefore, it is important to manage your immigration status carefully in order to
continue your studies and life in Korea in a stable manner.

passages.heading: What is a Change of Stay Status?
passages.text: This refers to situations where a foreigner residing in Korea wishes to stop activities related to their current stay status and engage in activities under a different stay status.

passages.heading: Cases for Application
passages.text:
- When registering as a foreign resident or reporting a domestic residence as an overseas Korean with a foreign national.
- When the address of a registered foreign resident or domestic residence reporter changes.
- When applying for a stay period extension.
- When applying for a stay status change (mandatory for short-term stay status changing to long-term stay status).
- When applying for a change to permanent residence status.

passages.heading: Application Period
passages.text: - Before the expiration date of the current stay period.

passages.heading: Overview and recommended steps
passages.text:
- Before departure, check your passport validity, residence-card validity, current authorized stay, and any pending visa/status application.
- The Ministry of Justice announced a re-entry permit exemption for many registered foreigners returning within one year; the exemption is limited by the remaining period of authorized stay and immigration exceptions. Confirm that the policy still applies to your status and travel dates.
- Do not assume an expired residence card or an extension application guarantees admission back into Korea.
- Ask immigration (1345) before international travel if your status is changing, renewal is pending, your residence card is lost, or you will be outside Korea for an extended period.
- Check the destination country’s entry/visa requirements, your airline’s document requirements, and any transit visa obligations.
- On return, carry passport, residence card where applicable, and evidence of student status if useful. Border officials make the final entry determination.

passages.heading: 1. Important rules at a glance
passages.text:
| Procedure | Key information |
| First foreigner registration | Generally within 90 days after entering Korea when intending to stay over 90 days. |
| Initial application | Use HiKorea visit reservation and apply at the immigration office with jurisdiction over residence; some universities coordinate group submissions. |
| Physical card fee | KRW 35,000 for issuance/reissuance since 1 January 2025; other immigration service fees can apply separately. |
| Lost card | Report loss on HiKorea to reduce misuse risk, then separately apply for reissuance promptly. |
| Stay renewal | Extend permitted period of stay BEFORE expiration; replacing the plastic card alone does not extend status. |
| Address change | Registered foreigners generally report their new residence within 15 days after moving. |
| Passport information | Report applicable changes; the passport-reporting deadline has special rules, so check the current HiKorea notice or 1345. |

Important distinction: “ARC renewal” is colloquial. Government immigration procedures distinguish extension of period of stay (체류기간 연장), reissuance of a residence card (등록증 재발급), and reporting changes to registration details (등록사항 변경신고).

passages.heading: 4. Extending period of stay (체류기간 연장)
passages.text:
A residence card is evidence of registered status. Its physical replacement is NOT the mechanism for permission to remain longer. A D-2 or D-4 student who needs to stay beyond the authorized expiry date must request extension of period of stay before expiry, with the evidence appropriate to the student and institution.

1. Check the authorized stay expiry date and current visa subtype; do not rely only on the plastic card’s appearance.
1. Ask the university international office whether it offers student-group extension or issues required enrollment, attendance and financial documents.
1. Check HiKorea for current eligibility for e-application or make a visit reservation.
1. Prepare passport, residence card, application form, fee, proof of enrollment and residence, and additional immigration-requested records.
1. Submit the application before the current permitted stay ends and follow any instructions for biometric/card updates or additional evidence.
Risk situations: taking leave of absence, withdrawing, graduating, changing universities, or ending a language program can affect the basis for student stay. Do not assume the printed expiry date guarantees permission after a change in academic status. Seek university and immigration advice promptly.

passages.heading: 5. Changes to registered information (등록사항 변경신고)
passages.text:
Students must distinguish changes in identity/passport records from changes in their place of stay. The required channel, evidence and reporting deadline differ.

| Change | Deadline / distinction | Action |
| Moved to a different residence (체류지 변경신고) | Generally within 15 days after moving for registered foreign residents. | Report via eligible HiKorea e-service, local government office or immigration office; provide new proof of residence. |
| New passport / passport number (여권정보 변경신고) | Special passport-reporting rules apply; do not automatically use the address deadline. | Older official Visa Navigator guidance mentions 45 days after passport issuance and a receipt-date exception; verify current rule and accepted proof. |
| Name, nationality, sex, date of birth or other registration particulars (등록사항 변경신고) | A reporting obligation can apply, often within a short statutory period. | Check exact trigger, deadline and required documentary evidence with immigration before submitting. |
| Change of visa status (체류자격 변경허가) | Permission generally needed before activities of the new status. | This is a status application, not merely a card-details update. |

For address-change details, link this article to the separate RAG article “Change of Address in South Korea”.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
International students have a maximum allowable
period of stay for each degree program, so it is
not possible to extend beyond that limit. If you
have taken a leave of absence from school for two
semesters (one year) or more and have left and
reentered the country, the period spent abroad
may be excluded from the calculation of your total
period of stay.

Please refer to the table below for the maximum
period of stay when planning your academic
schedule.

Category
Maximum Stay Period

Associate Degree
Up to 3 years
(up to 4 years for 4-year programs)

Bachelor’s Degree
Up to 6 years
(up to 7 years for 5-year programs)

Master’s Degree
Up to 5 years
(up to 6 years for 3-year programs)

Doctoral Degree
Up to 8 years
(up to 7 years for 2-year programs)

I’d like to transfer to another school. I’ve already
been admitted to a new school. Can I apply for a
school transfer?

In principle, you are not allowed to transfer
between schools in Korea. You must leave the
country, obtain a new visa, and then return.

However, you may apply for a school transfer
if the reason for changing schools is deemed
unavoidable. Note that the total period of stay
must not exceed each duration of studies at the
current school and the new school. If you are
dismissed from your current school and subject to
departure, you will not be permitted to transfer.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
91

I am currently a language trainee but plan to study
at a university. I’d like to apply for an interim visa
and I want to know the requirements.

You can apply for a visa called an interim visa if the
period between the end of your current stay and
the start of the new semester is three months or
less. To be eligible, you must meet all three of the
following requirements:

① A student in a language training program

who meets the visa extension requirements,
including attendance rate;

② A student who has successfully completed

the language training program and who has
been admitted to a degree program equivalent
to an associate degree or higher at the same
university. If the student is admitted to a
different university, the new school must be a
general university or higher;

③ A student with TOPIK score of Level 3 or higher,

or a student who has stayed in Korea for 18
months or longer with a Language Student visa
and with proven Korean language proficiency.

I have applied for foreign resident registration, but I
moved to my friend’s home and my home address
has changed. What should I do?

If your home address has changed, you must
report the change of residence within 15 days. If
you did not sign the residence contract yourself
and you are staying at a provided residence
instead, you must submit (1) the lease agreement,
(2) a confirmation letter stating that the residence
is being provided, and (3) a copy of the residence
provider’s (friend’s) ID card.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
<※ Source: Seoul Immigration Office>
※ As of September 2025. The translation is for reference only. Visa-related information is taken from

the original Korean text. The contents of this document are subject to change according to the latest
guidelines. For accurate information, please contact the Immigration Contact Center (1345).

Can I return to my home country during a leave of
absence from school?

For changes in academic status such as leave of
absence or graduation, your school is required to
report the change to the competent immigration
office.

Once the immigration office receives the report,
the student is regarded as not attending the
school and will be provided with departure guid-
ance. If the student has already left the country,
the Student visa will be terminated regardless
of any remaining period of stay. Therefore, the
student must obtain a new visa to reenter the
country.

I graduated in February. Can I leave the country for
a short period and return before the period of stay
expires, since it is valid until March?

The immigration office gets notified of the grad-
uation by the school and reviews the student’s
residence status. If the student has already left
the country, the Student visa will be considered
terminated regardless of any remaining period of
stay. Therefore, the visa will be terminated.

If you plan to pursue a higher degree or find em-
ployment in Korea after graduating from university,
we recommend extending your period of stay
or obtaining approval for a change of visa status
before leaving the country.

passages.heading: Deadline for Report
passages.text:
Within 15 days from the date of moving to a new residence.

※ Failure to report an address change within 15 days by a registered foreign resident constitutes a violation of Article 36 of the Immigration Act and may result in a fine of up to 1 million KRW.

passages.heading: Cases for Application
passages.text:
- When registering as a foreign resident or reporting a domestic residence as an overseas Korean with a foreign national.
- When the address of a registered foreign resident or domestic residence reporter changes.
- When applying for a stay period extension.
- When applying for a stay status change (mandatory for short-term stay status changing to long-term stay status).
- When applying for a change to permanent residence status.

passages.heading: Exceptions to Foreigner Registration
passages.text:
- The following foreigners are exempt from foreigner registration
- \- Diplomats, government officials, or individuals under agreements (A-1, A-2, A-3 visas).

- \- Nationals of Canada entering without a visa for stays of less than 6 months.

passages.heading: International Students
passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
The visa obtained by foreigners when searching for a job, preparing for an
internship, or starting a new business. It is categorized into General Job-Seeking
(D-10-1), Preparing Tech Start-Up (D-10-2), and Internship in Advanced Technology
(D-10-3). The following section describes the General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) visa.

General Job-Seeking (D-10-1)

The relevant visa allows applicants to seek fields of employment or complete
internships corresponding to eligibility for the Professor (E-1) to Special Occupa-
tion (E-7) visa upon graduation from a Korean university. After securing full-time
employment, the E-series visa generally requires conversion to an E-7 visa.

Allowed Period of Stay:
1 year. Extensions are possible for up to 3 years.
※However, please note that the length of stay may vary depending on individual eligibility.

Application Period:
It is required to apply for a change in the D-10-1 visa status as soon as possible
after graduation.

Eligible Applicants:
(1) Applicants Subject to the Point-based Review System

Applicants must hold at least a bachelor's degree—including a Korean university
associate's degree—as a legal resident in Korea, and have a total score of 60 or
more, with at least 20 points in the baseline items out of a total of 190 points on
the Job Search Score Sheet*
*The visa status is issued based on a points-based review system and must meet the score
requirements.
(2) Applicants Exempted from the Point-based Review System

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Can I begin my university degree with a D-4 visa?

A. Check whether a D-2 status change is required and secure approval before commencing activities requiring D-2.

Q. Does a job offer convert my visa automatically?

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

Q. Can everyone apply for D-10?

A. No. Eligibility and exclusions depend on individual history and criteria.

passages.heading: Duration for Job-Seeking Visa (D-10-1)
passages.text: The D-10-1 visa allows for internship programs before formal employment and is intended for job-seeking activities in professional fields corresponding to E-1 to E-7 qualifications. (Manual labor or unskilled work is not permitted.) Once employment is confirmed, the visa must be changed to one that aligns with the employment type.

passages.heading: What is a Job-Seeking Visa Change?
passages.text: This visa allows international students who have completed their studies in Korea or foreigners seeking new employment to legally stay in Korea. It must be changed to a job-seeking visa (D-10-1), which is issued to foreigners wishing to work in Korea.

passages.heading: Work-Learning Linked Study Visa (D-2-7) for Government Scholarship Students
passages.text:
Graduates with D-2-7 status are exempt from applying national employment ratios and company size restrictions when changing to E-7 (Specific Activity) status. Broader job categories are permitted.

passages.heading: 4. Extending period of stay (체류기간 연장)
passages.text:
A residence card is evidence of registered status. Its physical replacement is NOT the mechanism for permission to remain longer. A D-2 or D-4 student who needs to stay beyond the authorized expiry date must request extension of period of stay before expiry, with the evidence appropriate to the student and institution.

1. Check the authorized stay expiry date and current visa subtype; do not rely only on the plastic card’s appearance.
1. Ask the university international office whether it offers student-group extension or issues required enrollment, attendance and financial documents.
1. Check HiKorea for current eligibility for e-application or make a visit reservation.
1. Prepare passport, residence card, application form, fee, proof of enrollment and residence, and additional immigration-requested records.
1. Submit the application before the current permitted stay ends and follow any instructions for biometric/card updates or additional evidence.
Risk situations: taking leave of absence, withdrawing, graduating, changing universities, or ending a language program can affect the basis for student stay. Do not assume the printed expiry date guarantees permission after a change in academic status. Seek university and immigration advice promptly.

passages.text: Do not assume this. Academic-status changes can affect your D-2 status. Contact your university and immigration service promptly.

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
The visa obtained by foreigners when searching for a job, preparing for an
internship, or starting a new business. It is categorized into General Job-Seeking
(D-10-1), Preparing Tech Start-Up (D-10-2), and Internship in Advanced Technology
(D-10-3). The following section describes the General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) visa.

General Job-Seeking (D-10-1)

The relevant visa allows applicants to seek fields of employment or complete
internships corresponding to eligibility for the Professor (E-1) to Special Occupa-
tion (E-7) visa upon graduation from a Korean university. After securing full-time
employment, the E-series visa generally requires conversion to an E-7 visa.

Allowed Period of Stay:
1 year. Extensions are possible for up to 3 years.
※However, please note that the length of stay may vary depending on individual eligibility.

Application Period:
It is required to apply for a change in the D-10-1 visa status as soon as possible
after graduation.

Eligible Applicants:
(1) Applicants Subject to the Point-based Review System

Applicants must hold at least a bachelor's degree—including a Korean university
associate's degree—as a legal resident in Korea, and have a total score of 60 or
more, with at least 20 points in the baseline items out of a total of 190 points on
the Job Search Score Sheet*
*The visa status is issued based on a points-based review system and must meet the score
requirements.
(2) Applicants Exempted from the Point-based Review System

passages.heading: 5) Change in Visa Status
passages.text:
This refers to a situation wherein a foreign national residing in Korea intends to dis-
continue the activity permitted under his/her current visa and begin a new activity
that falls under a different visa category. <e.g., Student (D-2) → Job seeking (D-10)>

In principle, foreigners who intend to change their visa status must leave the coun-
try, obtain the new visa, and reenter Korea. Under limited circumstances, however,
a change of visa status may be allowed within Korea following a stringent review
process, provided the applicant meets the eligibility requirements for the new visa.

※ Permission for a change in visa status must be obtained from the competent Immigration

Office before engaging in any activity that falls under a different visa category

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
The visa obtained by foreigners when searching for a job, preparing for an
internship, or starting a new business. It is categorized into General Job-Seeking
(D-10-1), Preparing Tech Start-Up (D-10-2), and Internship in Advanced Technology
(D-10-3). The following section describes the General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) visa.

General Job-Seeking (D-10-1)

The relevant visa allows applicants to seek fields of employment or complete
internships corresponding to eligibility for the Professor (E-1) to Special Occupa-
tion (E-7) visa upon graduation from a Korean university. After securing full-time
employment, the E-series visa generally requires conversion to an E-7 visa.

Allowed Period of Stay:
1 year. Extensions are possible for up to 3 years.
※However, please note that the length of stay may vary depending on individual eligibility.

Application Period:
It is required to apply for a change in the D-10-1 visa status as soon as possible
after graduation.

Eligible Applicants:
(1) Applicants Subject to the Point-based Review System

Applicants must hold at least a bachelor's degree—including a Korean university
associate's degree—as a legal resident in Korea, and have a total score of 60 or
more, with at least 20 points in the baseline items out of a total of 190 points on
the Job Search Score Sheet*
*The visa status is issued based on a points-based review system and must meet the score
requirements.
(2) Applicants Exempted from the Point-based Review System

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
① Initial Visa Application after Graduation for International Students.

International students who graduated from an associate's degree program or
higher at a Korean university with a Student (D-2) visa and are changing to a
General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) visa for the first time after graduation.

② Graduates from a Korean university with excellent Korean language proficiency.

Applicants who have earned an associate's degree or higher from a Korean
university within the past 3 years and hold a valid TOPIK score of Level 4 or
higher, or have passed the interim evaluation for the Social Integration Program
(Level 4), including those assigned to Level 5 of the preliminary evaluation.

67

Required Documents:

(1) Eligibility for the Point-based Review System

Common documents: Valid passport, residence card (if applicable), fee, ID
photo, integrated application form, proof of residence, job search plan, diploma/
degree certificate, proof of funds for living expenses, other documents deemed
necessary for the point-based evaluation
Required to submit if applicable: Tuberculosis diagnosis, university transcript/
ranking document, employment certificate, Korean language proficiency
certificate, job recommendation letter, proof of high-income professional status

(2) Applicants exempted from the Point-based Review System

Common documents: Valid passport, residence card (if applicable), fee, ID
photo, integrated application form, proof of residence, job search plan, diploma
for associate’s degree or higher from a Korean university or diploma
Korean language proficiency certificate (Applicable only to Korean university
graduates with excellent Korean language proficiency)

※ Applicants for ‘Initial Visa Application after Graduation for International Students’ and ‘Grad-

passages.heading: 1) Job Seeker (D-10)
passages.text:
※ Applicants for ‘Initial Visa Application after Graduation for International Students’ and ‘Grad-

uates from a Korean university with excellent Korean language proficiency’ are exempt from
submission of proof of living expenses.

[Note for a General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) Visa Holders]

Internship Requirements

• Internships at the same employer during the valid D-10-1 visa period are
permitted one time, for up to 1 year.

• Internships involving unskilled labor or production jobs are not eligible.

• Holders must report to the competent Immigration Office within 15 days of
the first day of the internship (via fax or in-person visit).

※ Document Submissions: Copy of the passport and residence card, integrated

application form, internship employment contract, copy of the company’s business
registration certificate, and list of employees covered by employment Insurance.

Whether Eligible for Part-time Positions

In principle, international students are not allowed to engage in part-time
employment. However, they may work part-time within limited hours and
approved job categories after obtaining permission for part-time employment,
provided they meet certain requirements.

68

passages.heading: 2. Rules and eligibility
passages.text:
- Apply for change of stay status before engaging in activity that requires the new status.
- Changing from D-4 language training to D-2 study or D-2 graduation to D-10/E-series employment is not automatic.
- Application feasibility and supporting evidence depend on current visa subtype, destination visa subtype, academic achievements and immigration history.
- A university acceptance or employer offer is not the same as status-change approval.

passages.heading: 5. Frequently asked questions (retrieval targets)
passages.text:
Q. Can I begin my university degree with a D-4 visa?

A. Check whether a D-2 status change is required and secure approval before commencing activities requiring D-2.

Q. Does a job offer convert my visa automatically?

A. No. Immigration approval is required for a change of status when applicable.

Q. Can everyone apply for D-10?

A. No. Eligibility and exclusions depend on individual history and criteria.

passages.text:
89

I left the country after submitting a civil petition
to the immigration office. Can the office review
the matter while I’m overseas or handle it after I
reenter the country?

If an applicant is confirmed to have left the country
during the review process, the review will be
suspended or may be terminated at the discretion
of the immigration officer.

This is because the inquiry cannot remain unre-
solved for an extended period when it is uncertain
whether the applicant will return to the country,
and it is difficult to obtain additional information
when further confirmation is needed during the
review. Therefore, please make your inquiry with
your departure schedule in mind. In unavoidable
circumstances, you should submit the inquiry
again after reentering the country.

I plan to return to my home country after gradua-
tion, and this will terminate my visa. Is there a way
to get employed after I return to Korea?

We recommend obtaining approval for a visa
change before leaving the country if you plan to
look for a job after graduation or if your employ-
ment has already been confirmed.

If you do not have enough time, you may apply for
a Job Seeker (D-10) visa after leaving the country.
If this is your first Job Seeker (D-10) visa after
graduation and it is within one year of your grad-
uation date, you will be exempted from the point-
based system.

90

I have stayed in Korea for up to six years—which
is the maximum permitted period of stay—while
completing my bachelor’s degree program at a
university. However, I still need to have my thesis
reviewed. Can I extend my period of stay?

passages.heading: 2) Student (D-2)
passages.text:
Students must obtain a Student (D-2) visa to enroll in regular degree programs at
institutions of higher education in Korea, including associate, bachelor’s, master’s,
and doctoral degree programs.

Eligibility
Foreign nationals who intend to enroll in regular degree programs
or conduct specific research at the following educational institutions:

[Educational Institutions]

Universities or university-affiliated language institutes that meet
the requirements set by the Minister of Justice as educational
or research institutions being equivalent to or higher than junior
colleges established under the Higher Education Act or Special
Acts.

• (Exceptions) The following are excluded from educational
institutions attended by students eligible for the Student visa:
➀ Broadcasting universities, correspondence universities, open

universities, and cyber (online) universities as defined in
Article 2(5) of the Higher Education Act

➁ Lifelong education institutions as defined in Article 2(2) of the

Lifelong Education Act

19

➂ Vocational training programs among technical colleges as

defined in Article 2(5) of the National Lifelong Vocational Skills
Development Act

➃ Night colleges and graduate schools, excluding certain night

degree programs* eligible for student visas.
* Night graduate schools without daytime programs or night advanced

major programs at junior colleges that have undergone prior
screening for night degree programs by the competent immigration
office.

passages.heading: Duration for Job-Seeking Visa (D-10-1)
passages.text: The D-10-1 visa allows for internship programs before formal employment and is intended for job-seeking activities in professional fields corresponding to E-1 to E-7 qualifications. (Manual labor or unskilled work is not permitted.) Once employment is confirmed, the visa must be changed to one that aligns with the employment type.

passages.heading: 2) Eligibility
passages.text:
Students with a certain level of Korean proficiency who are committed to their
primary purpose of study (language training) and who have obtained approval from
the university staff in charge of international students

• Students holding the following visa types among all student visas: D-2-1 through
D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7

• Students whose visa status has changed from language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or
visiting student (D-2-8) and who have stayed in Korea for more than six months
since the date of status change (or since the date of entry for visa holders)
※ Students who have completed the regular education program at a university but do not

meet the graduation requirements (i.e., grades, attendance rate) and who have been

exceptionally permitted to stay as a result are not eligible.

• Among those who have completed a master’s or a doctoral program, however,
students who have received a special visa extension for the purpose of thesis
preparation are exceptionally permitted to work. The permitted working hours are
up to 30 hours per week, and unlimited permission does not apply during days
off, public holidays, and vacation periods.

passages.heading: 2) Eligibility
passages.text:
Students with a certain level of Korean proficiency who are committed to their
primary purpose of study (language training) and who have obtained approval from
the university staff in charge of international students

• Students holding the following visa types among all student visas: D-2-1 through
D-2-4, D-2-6, and D-2-7

• Students whose visa status has changed from language training (D-4-1, D-4-7) or
visiting student (D-2-8) and who have stayed in Korea for more than six months
since the date of status change (or since the date of entry for visa holders)
※ Students who have completed the regular education program at a university but do not

meet the graduation requirements (i.e., grades, attendance rate) and who have been

exceptionally permitted to stay as a result are not eligible.

• Among those who have completed a master’s or a doctoral program, however,
students who have received a special visa extension for the purpose of thesis
preparation are exceptionally permitted to work. The permitted working hours are
up to 30 hours per week, and unlimited permission does not apply during days
off, public holidays, and vacation periods.

[Note for a General Job-Seeking (D-10-1) Visa Holders]

Internship Requirements

• Internships at the same employer during the valid D-10-1 visa period are
permitted one time, for up to 1 year.

• Internships involving unskilled labor or production jobs are not eligible.

• Holders must report to the competent Immigration Office within 15 days of
the first day of the internship (via fax or in-person visit).

※ Document Submissions: Copy of the passport and residence card, integrated

application form, internship employment contract, copy of the company’s business
registration certificate, and list of employees covered by employment Insurance.

Whether Eligible for Part-time Positions

In principle, international students are not allowed to engage in part-time
employment. However, they may work part-time within limited hours and
approved job categories after obtaining permission for part-time employment,
provided they meet certain requirements.

passages.heading: 1. Part-Time Employment
passages.text:
In principle, foreign residents with a student visa are prohibited from engaging
in employment other than studying. However, international students who obtain
permission from the head of their affiliated university or the competent Immigration
Office may engage in part-time employment for a designated period while pursuing
their studies.

Part-time employment is limited to activities typically performed by students, who
must obtain prior approval before beginning part-time work.

※ Foreign residents who engage in employment without valid authorization or violate

the conditions of the granted permission may face administrative sanctions such
as fines, penalties, or deportation.

※ Students who are interested in engaging in employment activities specified in

Table 1-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Immigration Act, individual guidelines
for each visa category will apply (e.g., Presidential English Program scholarship
recipients, foreign language instructors, and professional interpreters/transla-
tors).

※ Private tutoring is strictly prohibited, considering the specificity of the activity,

such as location and target.
